adjusted_gap.assumptions: TRANWORK codes the primary means of transportation last week, so hybrid workers who mostly commute count as commuters; hourly wages use weeks-worked interval midpoints and state top-coded wage income as released; no causal interpretation.
adjusted_gap.estimand: The population linear-projection coefficient on working from home (TRANWORK = 80) in a regression of log hourly wage on WFH, age, age², sex, and four education levels. A descriptive adjusted contrast between WFH workers and commuters, not the causal effect of working from home.
adjusted_gap.estimator: WLS with PERWT on 984,475 person records; OLS with equal case weights reported alongside.
adjusted_gap.explicit_weights: PERWT, the ACS person weight: base weight adjusted for noninterview and calibrated to Census population estimates. Equal case weights in the OLS comparison.
adjusted_gap.implicit_weights: Within education groups, the coefficient averages WFH–commuter contrasts with weights proportional to population share × p(1 − p), where p is the WFH share; high-overlap groups count most (Chapter 5).
adjusted_gap.randomness: The ACS sample of addresses and the response process. WFH is not assigned by any design.
adjusted_gap.target_population: Wage and salary workers aged 25–64 in the 2024 ACS who usually worked 30+ hours a week for 40+ weeks in the past 12 months, had positive wage income, and were at work in the reference week; about 105 million people.
adjusted_gap.title: Do people who work from home earn more? The adjusted contrast (ACS 2024)
adjusted_gap.variance_estimator: Successive difference replication with 80 replicate weights: Var = (4/80)Σ(β_r − β)², df = 79.

occupation_adjusted.assumptions: Occupation and industry are measured for the main job; controlling for them conditions on outcomes of the same choices that shape WFH, so the contrast is not a structural wage premium.
occupation_adjusted.estimand: The population linear-projection coefficient on WFH after adding fixed effects for detailed occupation, industry, and state: a WFH–commuter contrast among workers with the same recorded job and location, still descriptive.
occupation_adjusted.estimator: WLS with PERWT and 841 fixed-effect dummies, solved as sparse normal equations.
occupation_adjusted.explicit_weights: PERWT (ACS person weight). Equal case weights for OLS.
occupation_adjusted.implicit_weights: A linear probability model for WFH with additive fixed effects; about 9% of weighted commuters get negative implied weight because their predicted WFH probability is below zero (Chapter 5).
occupation_adjusted.randomness: The ACS sample and response process.
occupation_adjusted.target_population: Wage and salary workers aged 25–64 in the 2024 ACS who usually worked 30+ hours a week for 40+ weeks in the past 12 months, had positive wage income, and were at work in the reference week.
occupation_adjusted.title: The same contrast within occupation, industry, and state
occupation_adjusted.variance_estimator: SDR, 80 replicates, each a full re-solve of the fixed-effect normal equations; df = 79.
